top.title: Caitlin Clark publicly questions Dallas Cowboys after embarrassing Thanksgiving loss
top.description: Credit: Ron Jenkins/Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are getting criticised from all angles, and even WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark couldn’t resist questioning what went wrong on Thanksgiving. The Dallas Cowboys suffered one of the most embarrassing comeback losses at the hands of the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. Despite having a 31-10 lead in the third quarter, they gave up nearly 30 points in the final quarter and a half to lose the game 39-38. The Cowboys’ misery was compounded by the fact that Philly was led by their own former player in Joe Milton III. The 26-year-old was on the same wavelength as DeVonta Smith, who had two touchdowns and 200 yards on the day. The entire situation naturally led to a lot of mockery and criticism for Dallas on social media, and even superstars from other leagues couldn’t resist. Caitlin Clark questions what the Cowboys were doing during their 4th quarter collapse Thanksgiving is all about the NFL when it comes to the world of sports, and the games have not disappointed in the slightest. That also means more people are tuned in than they are for the rest of the season. Caitlin Clark was also clearly watching this year. After the Cowboys fell apart in the fourth quarter, Clark was in disbelief much like the rest of the country, and she shared her bemusement on social media. “What exactly were the Cowboys doing there?” Clark asked in a post on X. She isn’t exactly known for posting regularly on the platform either, which just goes to show how wild what happened during the Dallas game was. This is unfortunately just the beginning for the 5-7 Cowboys. A loss like this doesn’t just go away, and especially not when it happens on a stage this big. There will be plenty of time for assessing everything that went wrong, but for now, Dallas will simply have to deal with all the mockery. Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark had a one-line question for the Dallas Cowboys after their 39-38 Thanksgiving loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas let a 21-point lead slip away at AT&T Stadium, with Jake Elliott winning it for Philadelphia on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. The Eagles also had an unexpected contributor in quarterback Joe Milton, who started against his former team after joining Philadelphia from Dallas’ practice squad in October. Chiefs Fan Caitlin Clark Has a Question for the Cowboys After Thanksgiving Collapse The three-time WNBA All-Star has long supported the Kansas City Chiefs, who also played on Thanksgiving, but her attention turned to the Cowboys-Eagles game. She wrote : “What exactly were the Cowboys doing there?” Clark didn’t specify which moment prompted the question. Clark has made her NFL loyalties clear before, including during an appearance on Kylie Kelce’s podcast earlier this month. On the November 3 episode of “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce,” host Kylie Kelce brought up the Colts jersey Clark had passed on wearing, despite the Fever sharing Indianapolis with the NFL team. Clark said she hadn’t initially thought about upsetting Chiefs fans or Travis Kelce by wearing the jersey. However, she realized afterward that her teammates had worn theirs. She put it plainly : “I am diehard Chiefs. top.title: Christian Mahogany, Dan Campbell Address Costly Taunting Penalty in Detroit Lions Loss to Bears
top.description: For a moment, it looked like Jahmyr Gibbs had delivered the knockout blow in the Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Chicago Bears. With 8:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, Gibbs exploded for a 70-yard touchdown run that put the Lions in position to take a 12-point lead. Unfortunately, what happened immediately after the touchdown proved costly. Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany was flagged for taunting, resulting in a 15-yard penalty that pushed Jake Bates’ extra-point attempt back to 48 yards. Bates missed the kick, and what could have been a relatively insignificant penalty ended up having a major impact on how the remainder of the game unfolded. Christian Mahogany Takes Responsibility for Costly Penalty Following Detroit’s 39-35 loss to Chicago, Mahogany acknowledged that he allowed Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to get under his skin. Rather than making excuses for his actions, Mahogany admitted that he failed to keep his emotions in check. “I feel bad that that happened,” Mahogany told reporters in the locker room. “I just got too hot and too high and let my emotions get the best of me.” Mahogany’s comments came on the same afternoon that he accused the Bears of simulating Jared Goff’s snap count . Clearly, there was no love lost between Mahogany and Simmons throughout Thursday’s divisional showdown. Detroit Lions’ head coach Dan Campbell looks over plan with defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard during the first half of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. The Bears converted the ensuing two-point attempt, cutting Detroit’s lead to 35-32 rather than 36-32. Greg Rousseau tallies his 11th sack of the season 💪 KCvsBUF on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hBKaqwPgjQ — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 Williams spent four seasons (2012-2015) in Buffalo, recording double-digit sacks in each of his first three years with the team. His best season came in 2014 when he recorded 14.5 sacks and earned first-team All-Pro honors. Rousseau, now in his sixth NFL season, has spent his entire career in Buffalo after the Bills selected him with the 30th overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Having already established a new personal single-season record for sacks this year , the 26 year old is now working his way through some familiar names in Buffalo’s history books. Once Rousseau gets past Mario Williams, there’s another Williams waiting for him. Former defensive tackle Kyle Williams (48.5), who spent all 13 of his NFL seasons in Buffalo, sits sixth on the franchise’s all-time list. With six regular-season games remaining, and the way Rousseau has been getting to opposing quarterbacks lately, we might not have to wait until next season to talk about him catching another Williams.

Herbstreit’s ESPN contract runs out once this college football season ends, and the network’s response pointed to fuller talks after the season, with ESPN hoping to land a new deal then. Fans who weighed in on the news Thursday, however, showed little appetite for a new contract at all, and several wanted ESPN to move on. ESPN Eyes Kirk Herbstreit Talks After the College Football Season ESPN’s statement cooled talk that a deal was near. “We’re not close to an agreement,” a spokesperson for the network told Front Office Sports. “We have communicated to Kirk’s team that we are prepared to engage more directly after the college football season, and we’re hopeful we can get something done at that time.” Herbstreit did not immediately get back to Front Office Sports when it asked for comment. ESPN’s timeline matches what Andrew Marchand reported in September: that ESPN would hold off on talks with Herbstreit until the offseason. Herbstreit joined the College GameDay cast in 1996 and took over as the network’s lead college football game analyst in 2006. top.title: James Cook makes NFL history on Thanksgiving night
top.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 26: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball while being chased by Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs in the second quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. James Cook III has now rushed for 75+ yards and a TD in 10 consecutive games, extending his record for the longest single-season streak in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/TbTrvIPiQb — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 27, 2026 Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night during the second quarter to put the Bills up 7-0 . He then eclipsed the 75-yard mark in the third quarter on a five-yard run that put him at 79 for the night. JIMBO!!! 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/83xqEMHxZ8 — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 27, 2026 It’s been 30 years since Allen put together his streak of 10 games. Since then, we’ve watched some pretty impressive running backs come through the NFL. LaDainian Tomlinson, Adrian Peterson, and Derrick Henry have all had their share of record-setting performances, but none of them managed to do what Cook just did. And unlike Allen, who needed parts of two seasons to put together his streak, Cook has done it all in the same season. In fact, the Bills’ season opener was the only game this year in which Cook didn’t meet both statistical requirements. Cook entered Thursday night’s game having rushed for 1,003 yards and 10 touchdowns over the course of his nine-game streak, averaging 111.4 yards per game and 5.1 yards per carry. He eclipsed the century mark in five of those nine games, including a season-high 157-yard performance against the New York Jets. Remember when we spent so much of the offseason in 2025 talking about whether the Bills should pay Cook? Buffalo eventually gave its running back a four-year, $48 million contract extension, and Cook has spent the better part of two seasons giving us reasons to talk about what a good decision that was. The Bills will head to Foxborough next week for their second meeting of the season with the New England Patriots. Cook rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in their first matchup. Another 75 yards and a trip to the end zone next week, and Cook will have an NFL record all to himself. Considering we’ve been watching him do just that every week since September, it might be time to start wondering just how big a number he’s going to leave for the next running back to chase.

top.title: Skip Bayless says what he ‘feared’ about Joe Milton actually came true during Cowboys vs Eagles
top.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles star Joe Milton was the star of the show in his first game against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys. The quarterback was demoted to the practice squad by Dallas after an underwhelming pre-season. The Eagles picked him up, and his recent performances have made that decision look like a masterstroke. Milton was outstanding on Thanksgiving in the 39-38 comeback win for Philadelphia, and Skip Bayless has now claimed that he saw this coming. Skip Bayless says he feared Joe Milton would come back to haunt the Dallas Cowboys Milton had a fantastic game against the Dallas Cowboys. The 26-year-old had impressed in his first two starts against the Giants and the Steelers, but he didn’t manage a single touchdown pass in those appearances. However, against his old team, he scored four total scores on Thanksgiving and was one of the best players on the field. Bayless was hoping that Milton would not come back to haunt the Cowboys, but his worst fears came true, and Dallas ended up losing despite leading for most of the game. The TV presenter said in a video on X: “I did say on Friday’s Gridiron, I feared Joe Milton. He’s Josh Allen. He’s 6’5″, 240, ran 4’6”, coming out of Tennessee, and he’s got a huge arm. Yet, he never displayed consistent accuracy or poise in Cowboys pre-season games. “I said he’ll probably come back and he’ll be on a mission to prove us wrong – we demoted him and they took him from our practice squad. He had the game of his life. “And he looked like Josh Allen. He looked like Josh Allen plus Brock Purdy against the Vikings. He didn’t miss anything. It was just sensational.” Bayless posted a series of tweets during the game, and he showered Milton with praise, comparing him to Josh Allen and claiming that the quarterback was ‘torching the team that demoted him’. The Eagles star finished the game with 21 of 31 passes completed for 331 yards, three passing touchdowns and an interception, while adding 15 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown. It’s still early days for Milton, who has only started three games, but the signs are really positive, and he could make a big difference for the Eagles if he continues playing in the same way. top.title: Beckham Black, No. 1 Basketball Recruit, Cancels Duke Visit
top.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Beckham Black ’s recruitment took another turn Tuesday, with the five-star guard no longer expected to make a scheduled visit to Duke. Black, the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2027 Rivals Industry Rankings, had been expected to attend the Blue Devils’ Nov. 17 matchup against Illinois. The visit was removed from his schedule, according to Jon Van Hoozer of High School On SI . No reason for the cancellation was reported, and there is no indication that Black has ruled out Duke. For now, it is a change to his recruiting itinerary, not necessarily a shift in his list of contenders. Black Has Visited Several National Powers Black has already taken visits to Texas, North Carolina, Florida, Arkansas and Georgetown, according to Rivals. That list features some of the biggest names in college basketball, with programs from the SEC, ACC and Big East getting an opportunity to make their pitch to the five-star prospect. Duke was next on the schedule. The cancellation leaves the Blue Devils without that planned opportunity, but it does not tell the full story of where they stand in his recruitment. Black remains one of the top uncommitted players in the 2027 class, and his next recruiting move will be worth watching as his senior season progresses. Black’s Production at Southeastern Prep Speaks for Itself While the recruiting picture remains unsettled, Black has been putting up big numbers at Southeastern Prep in Orlando. The school lists him at 21.1 points, 6.5 rebounds and 9.4 assists per game through 11 appearances. He has shown the ability to take over as a scorer while also creating opportunities for his teammates. Black poured in 33 points and dished out nine assists in a 78-77 win over Prince George’s Christian on Nov. 13. A day later, he recorded 15 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists in an 80-65 victory against Cats Academy. He also posted 20 points and 20 assists against the Diamond Doves earlier in November. On Oct. 30, Black delivered one of his biggest performances of the season, finishing with 45 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists against BC Dubai. Those numbers show why Black is viewed as one of the premier prospects in the country. He can score at a high level, but his playmaking makes him an even more difficult matchup. Black Has Built a National Profile Black’s résumé extends beyond his high school production. He has won two gold medals with USA Basketball and is the younger brother of NBA guard Anthony Black. Originally from Duncanville, Texas, he has continued to build his profile at Southeastern Prep. Rivals reported that Black averaged 21.7 points, 5.4 assists, four rebounds and 1.7 steals on the EYBL circuit over the summer. For now, his college destination remains unknown. Duke’s canceled visit adds another wrinkle to a recruitment that already includes several prominent programs, but Black’s next decision will offer a clearer picture of where things stand. top.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton (14) smiles as he talks with Fox’s Tom Rinaldi after winning an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington. (Elías Valverde II/The Dallas Morning News) ARLINGTON — Eagles backup quarterback Joe Milton was smiling when he met the media late Thursday afternoon. Milton completed 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the Eagles' dramatic 39-38 victory over the Cowboys . For Milton, it wasn’t a time to gloat, considering he spent nearly two seasons with the Cowboys as a backup quarterback. But it was hard not to notice the smile. “I know that defense like the back of my hand,” Milton said. Dallas Cowboys fans Liza Cruz holds hands with her daughter Ashley Adauto as they record a video dressed as turkeys before an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington. The only thing you can do is just prepare yourself and that’s just the main thing I did.” Milton got his revenge, leading a six-play, 11-yard drive that took 48 seconds to set up kicker Jake Elliott for a game-winning 59-yard field goal with seven seconds to play. It was part of a 22-point fourth quarter where Milton completed 8 of 13 passes for 111 yards with a touchdown pass and a touchdown run. nigeria.description: By Esther Onyegbulam, Matthew Johnson & Patrick Chidubem Six persons were burnt to death, while 12 others sustained varying degrees of burns yesterday after a commercial vehicle caught fire at Magbon, along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, which confirmed the incident, said the victims comprised two females and four males, all adults. It added that the 12 injured persons were rescued and taken to Badagry General Hospital for medical attention. However, an eyewitness account shared in a video gave a different initial account of the tragedy, claiming that many people were feared dead, with only two occupants, reportedly the driver and another passenger, surviving the incident. According to the eyewitness, the accident occurred between 8am and 9am and involved a commercial bus travelling from Mile 2 towards Badagry. The incident reportedly happened shortly after Checking Point Bus Stop, before the Black Signboard axis of the expressway. The eyewitness account indicated that the vehicle caught fire, resulting in multiple casualties. However, the initial casualty figures could not be independently verified. In its official account, the Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 8:44am, while firefighters from its Badagry station arrived at the scene at 9:13am. According to Adeseye, “Preliminary information gathered during the investigation indicated that the driver reportedly had an additional five litres of fuel stored inside the vehicle, intending to refuel the vehicle’s tank. The presence of the extra fuel is suspected to have contributed to the intensity of the fire. “Tragically, six persons, comprising two females and four males, all adults, were involved in the incident. All six victims were burnt beyond recognition,” the statement said. Vanguard News The post How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident appeared first on Vanguard News .

The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. Describing the milestone as more than a numerical achievement, she said the centre remained committed to delivering services with dignity and respect. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors and had engaged an independent consultant to assess its services, identify gaps and recommend improvements. She thanked the centre’s partners and funders, assuring that it would continue to provide compassionate care where survivors’ voices mattered. nigeria.title: 18.3m children out of school: Stakeholders demand urgent action
nigeria.description: … NGE challenges govt, media, private sector as UNICEF warns on first 1,000 days By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners yesterday called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million children out of school in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF Representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. This came as the Federal Government assured voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties of protection before, during and after the elections. Speaking at a Strategic Election Security Conference jointly convened by INEC and the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, Amupitan said Nigeria had witnessed a disturbing escalation in political intolerance, inflammatory rhetoric and coordinated attacks since the commencement of campaigns in August 2026. Addressing political parties, he said: “Signing peace accords in Abuja while tolerating or financing thuggery in the states is a contradiction our democracy can no longer afford.” He warned that INEC would not succumb to threats or intimidation. “We will neither be intimidated nor blackmailed into compromising our neutrality, and every attack on INEC personnel, facilities, or materials will be met with the full weight of the law,” INEC chairman said. Amupitan said responsibility for electoral violence extended beyond those directly involved in attacks, stressing that political party leaders must be held accountable for the conduct of their candidates and supporters. He said: “Accountability does not end with the foot soldiers who throw stones or wield weapons,” adding that “party leadership bears moral and political responsibility for the conduct of its candidates, campaign councils, and youth wings”. nigeria.title: Kitto violence: Majority of victims suffer in silence – ISHRAI warns
nigeria.description: .. Only 28% of victims report attacks, survey across six South-West states reveals By Chioma Obinna A growing pattern of online deception, blackmail, sexual exploitation and extortion is exposing young Nigerians and other vulnerable people to physical attacks, psychological trauma and even death, with a survey revealing that 71.3 per cent of respondents across six South-West states had experienced Kitto-related violence. The survey also revealed that only 28 per cent of those affected reported their experiences, highlighting the extent of underreporting and the fear, stigma and discrimination that prevent victims from seeking help. The Improved Sexual Health and Rights Advocacy Initiative (ISHRAI), which disclosed the findings, raised the alarm over the trend, warning that victims were increasingly exposed to kidnapping, sexual abuse, blackmail, mob attacks and other forms of violence. The organisation called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, women and youth groups to intensify community awareness, protect vulnerable people and discourage public shaming, discrimination and jungle justice. Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement involving traditional and religious leaders, ISHRAI’s Programme Manager, Mrs Sophia Lawal, said community leaders must be equipped with the knowledge and referral mechanisms to identify cases of Kitto-related violence and respond appropriately. Lawal said the engagement brought together 20 traditional and religious leaders, including women leaders, to deliberate on the threats facing marginalised people and develop community-based responses. “It’s very important that we have community members, that’s the religious, traditional leaders, and also the women leaders, to have conversations around kitto violence that affects marginalized people in Nigeria,” she said. “And we cannot address these issues without having the right people in the room to deliberate on this matter together so that they are equipped with the right, with the knowledge to actually handle such cases when they are being reported or how to even identify such cases in their immediate community.” Providing details of the survey, an ISHRAI representative said 240 people were interviewed across the six South-West states, with 71.3 per cent indicating that they had experienced Kitto-related violence. He said the organisation’s intervention was aimed at reducing the practice through public education, early identification and effective community response. nigeria.title: ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt
nigeria.description: The Lagos State Government has dismissed rumours of a postponement of the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, confirming that it will hold across the state on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The exercise is scheduled to take place between 6:30am and 8:30am and will be monitored by government officials across various local government areas and local council development areas. The state government made the clarification on Thursday in a statement signed by Kunle Adeshina, Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources. The statement quoted the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, as saying there was no basis for postponing the exercise. “There is no basis to cancel the monthly exercise which has become a rallying point for everyone to stay back and clean their neighbourhood,” Tajudeen said. He added that the November edition would be monitored across the state, as had become a tradition. According to the statement, the First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, will lead a team of government officials to monitor the exercise in Eti-Osa Local Government Area. Similarly, another team led by the Head of Service, Mr Olabode Agoro, will monitor activities in Coker-Aguda Local Council Development Area. Explaining the timing of the exercise, Tajudeen said the 6:30am to 8:30am schedule would allow residents to participate in the clean-up without disrupting other activities. He said the timeframe “gives enough room for any form of civic exercise to still be undertaken after the clean-up.” The permanent secretary urged Lagos residents to remain in their neighbourhoods and participate actively in the exercise. He also called on transport unions to use the opportunity to clean their parks and garages before resuming passenger operations at 8:30am. The state government reiterated its call for collective participation in maintaining environmental cleanliness across Lagos State. nigeria.title: 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence
nigeria.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police, Hope Urunwa Okafor, has warned political parties and their leaders against violence, thuggery and hate speech ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okafor gave the warning during a meeting she convened with leaders and representatives of political parties in the state to discuss strategies for ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the elections. The meeting was attended by representatives of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party. The police commissioner reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force remained apolitical and impartial in the discharge of its duties. She assured the party leaders that the command was prepared to provide adequate security for campaign activities, protect lives and property, and maintain law and order across the state. Okafor stressed that no society could thrive in an atmosphere of violence, urging political parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech, personal attacks and other forms of communication capable of inciting violence. She charged party leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by ensuring that their words and actions promoted peaceful political engagement. The commissioner also urged them to demonstrate zero tolerance for violence among their supporters, rather than merely preaching peace. She called on the political parties to exercise restraint in their public statements and campaign activities and provide the command with timely information on their campaign schedules and other political engagements to enable adequate security arrangements. In their separate remarks, the party representatives commended the commissioner for convening the meeting, describing it as timely and necessary ahead of the 2027 elections. They appealed to the police command to provide adequate security during campaigns and other political activities. The party representatives also requested that candidates contesting various elective positions be invited to similar engagements to strengthen collective efforts towards peaceful elections. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
nigeria.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. business.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. entertainment.title: Remembering Pete Edochie: 5 Films That Made Him a Nollywood Legend
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.description: ‘Please Don’t Get It Done,’ ‘Everybody Hates Him’ — CFB Fans React to ESPN Being ‘Not Close to an Agreement’ With Kirk Herbstreit Over New Contract ESPN pushed back Wednesday on a Front Office Sports report by Ryan Glasspiegel that the network was nearing a long-term extension with Kirk Herbstreit, its lead college football analyst. Herbstreit’s ESPN contract runs out once this college football season ends, and the network’s response pointed to fuller talks after the season, with ESPN hoping to land a new deal then. Fans who weighed in on the news Thursday, however, showed little appetite for a new contract at all, and several wanted ESPN to move on. ESPN Eyes Kirk Herbstreit Talks After the College Football Season ESPN’s statement cooled talk that a deal was near. “We’re not close to an agreement,” a spokesperson for the network told Front Office Sports. “We have communicated to Kirk’s team that we are prepared to engage more directly after the college football season, and we’re hopeful we can get something done at that time.” Herbstreit did not immediately get back to Front Office Sports when it asked for comment. ESPN’s timeline matches what Andrew Marchand reported in September: that ESPN would hold off on talks with Herbstreit until the offseason. Herbstreit joined the College GameDay cast in 1996 and took over as the network’s lead college football game analyst in 2006. One fan answered the contract news with a joke, writing, “I’m sure Kirk wants his dog included somehow.” Another fan took a different route, offering ESPN an alternative for the job and pitching another candidate. “I know another former college QB who would love that gig. sports.title: James Cook makes NFL history on Thanksgiving night
sports.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 26: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball while being chased by Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs in the second quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. James Cook III has now rushed for 75+ yards and a TD in 10 consecutive games, extending his record for the longest single-season streak in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/TbTrvIPiQb — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 27, 2026 Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night during the second quarter to put the Bills up 7-0 . He then eclipsed the 75-yard mark in the third quarter on a five-yard run that put him at 79 for the night. JIMBO!!! 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/83xqEMHxZ8 — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 27, 2026 It’s been 30 years since Allen put together his streak of 10 games. Since then, we’ve watched some pretty impressive running backs come through the NFL. LaDainian Tomlinson, Adrian Peterson, and Derrick Henry have all had their share of record-setting performances, but none of them managed to do what Cook just did. And unlike Allen, who needed parts of two seasons to put together his streak, Cook has done it all in the same season. In fact, the Bills’ season opener was the only game this year in which Cook didn’t meet both statistical requirements. Cook entered Thursday night’s game having rushed for 1,003 yards and 10 touchdowns over the course of his nine-game streak, averaging 111.4 yards per game and 5.1 yards per carry. He eclipsed the century mark in five of those nine games, including a season-high 157-yard performance against the New York Jets. Remember when we spent so much of the offseason in 2025 talking about whether the Bills should pay Cook? Buffalo eventually gave its running back a four-year, $48 million contract extension, and Cook has spent the better part of two seasons giving us reasons to talk about what a good decision that was. The Bills will head to Foxborough next week for their second meeting of the season with the New England Patriots. Cook rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in their first matchup. Another 75 yards and a trip to the end zone next week, and Cook will have an NFL record all to himself. Considering we’ve been watching him do just that every week since September, it might be time to start wondering just how big a number he’s going to leave for the next running back to chase.

sports.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles star Joe Milton was the star of the show in his first game against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys. The quarterback was demoted to the practice squad by Dallas after an underwhelming pre-season. The Eagles picked him up, and his recent performances have made that decision look like a masterstroke. Milton was outstanding on Thanksgiving in the 39-38 comeback win for Philadelphia, and Skip Bayless has now claimed that he saw this coming. Skip Bayless says he feared Joe Milton would come back to haunt the Dallas Cowboys Milton had a fantastic game against the Dallas Cowboys. The 26-year-old had impressed in his first two starts against the Giants and the Steelers, but he didn’t manage a single touchdown pass in those appearances. sports.title: Beckham Black, No. 1 Basketball Recruit, Cancels Duke Visit
sports.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Beckham Black ’s recruitment took another turn Tuesday, with the five-star guard no longer expected to make a scheduled visit to Duke. Black, the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2027 Rivals Industry Rankings, had been expected to attend the Blue Devils’ Nov. 17 matchup against Illinois. The visit was removed from his schedule, according to Jon Van Hoozer of High School On SI . No reason for the cancellation was reported, and there is no indication that Black has ruled out Duke. For now, it is a change to his recruiting itinerary, not necessarily a shift in his list of contenders. Black Has Visited Several National Powers Black has already taken visits to Texas, North Carolina, Florida, Arkansas and Georgetown, according to Rivals. That list features some of the biggest names in college basketball, with programs from the SEC, ACC and Big East getting an opportunity to make their pitch to the five-star prospect. Duke was next on the schedule. The cancellation leaves the Blue Devils without that planned opportunity, but it does not tell the full story of where they stand in his recruitment. Black remains one of the top uncommitted players in the 2027 class, and his next recruiting move will be worth watching as his senior season progresses. Black’s Production at Southeastern Prep Speaks for Itself While the recruiting picture remains unsettled, Black has been putting up big numbers at Southeastern Prep in Orlando. The school lists him at 21.1 points, 6.5 rebounds and 9.4 assists per game through 11 appearances. He has shown the ability to take over as a scorer while also creating opportunities for his teammates. Black poured in 33 points and dished out nine assists in a 78-77 win over Prince George’s Christian on Nov. 13. A day later, he recorded 15 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists in an 80-65 victory against Cats Academy. He also posted 20 points and 20 assists against the Diamond Doves earlier in November. On Oct. 30, Black delivered one of his biggest performances of the season, finishing with 45 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists against BC Dubai. Those numbers show why Black is viewed as one of the premier prospects in the country. He can score at a high level, but his playmaking makes him an even more difficult matchup. Black Has Built a National Profile Black’s résumé extends beyond his high school production. He has won two gold medals with USA Basketball and is the younger brother of NBA guard Anthony Black. Originally from Duncanville, Texas, he has continued to build his profile at Southeastern Prep. Rivals reported that Black averaged 21.7 points, 5.4 assists, four rebounds and 1.7 steals on the EYBL circuit over the summer. For now, his college destination remains unknown. Duke’s canceled visit adds another wrinkle to a recruitment that already includes several prominent programs, but Black’s next decision will offer a clearer picture of where things stand. technology.title: The token factory never sleeps
technology.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. technology.description: Travel giant Flight Centre Travel Group (FLT) says "a significant number of customer records" may have been accessed by "unknown persons" following a cyberattack. The Brisbane-headquartered company said the incident affected a third-party accommodation booking system used by Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and some independent travel agents. Its disclosure [PDF], filed with the Australian Securities Exchange today, added that it was aware that records were accessed, but cannot definitively say how many were exfiltrated. Flight Centre is working with the supplier and incident response specialist Mandiant to establish the scope of the incident. An initial review suggests most accessed records contained only customer names, some with basic travel information. A "very small percentage" may also include birth dates, email addresses, limited passport details, phone numbers, or, in rare cases, health or mobility information. Flight bookings and corporate travel use separate systems and are unaffected, the company said. "FLT values customer privacy and data security," the company said in its disclosure. "The company understands that an incident like this can be unsettling for customers who may be affected, and we apologize for any concern this causes." Investigations remain ongoing, but FLT has already contained the attack, rotated keys and credentials, and increased system monitoring, it said. The company said it would contact affected customers directly. Its brands continue to operate normally, and travelers should proceed with their plans. technology.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
technology.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

technology.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
technology.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®

technology.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
technology.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated. Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft , a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too. The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning. However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account. So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them. “Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.” The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them. By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again. Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®

science.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
science.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease.
